name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 partisan lean in a Texas Panhandle seat
Jackson's $5.4M war chest vs. Nair's $14K cash on hand
Incumbent running with no polling or expert attention, consistent with a noncompetitive race
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Ronny Jackson's incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage (over $5.4 million to $14,000) make a Democratic upset implausible; markets price Jackson at about 95%. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move materially off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major national Democratic wave environment could tighten the race, though even then the margin is very large.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-13 is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, covering the Texas Panhandle with a partisan lean of R+23. Incumbent Ronny Jackson is seeking reelection with a large financial edge, holding $5.4 million on hand after raising over $4 million. Democratic challenger Mark Nair has raised about $102,000 with only $14,000 remaining, and no outside spending has been reported on his behalf.

Prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 95% chance of winning, and no polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican victory in the low-to-mid twenty-point range, with only modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
